recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Hundreds of galaxies, from white to yellow to deep red, fill this Webb view of El Gordo, Spanish for “the Fat One.” It was the most massive galaxy cluster known at its point in cosmic history, when the universe was 6.2 billion years old.

All that mass bends space around it, so El Gordo acts as a gravitational lens, stretching and magnifying the light of galaxies far behind it. Look for a long, thin line near the center running from about ten o'clock to four o'clock, nicknamed the Thin One, and a red swoosh at upper right called the Fishhook. Both are distorted images of distant background galaxies.

Hubble's earlier pictures only hinted at these features. Webb's infrared sight reveals dusty, distant objects here that had never been seen before, some of them stretched or even mirrored by the lens.

understand.summary: Webb's NIRCam combined six infrared filters from 1.15 to 4.44 microns, with the shortest shown in blue, the middle in green and the longest in red.
understand.eye: This is all infrared light, which the eye cannot see; the colors map it to visible hues, longest wavelengths reddest.
